principles.principle: Rank by harm. A crash beats a naming problem, every time.
One severity scale. Never invent a synonym mid-report.
Say must-fix or nice-to-have. Never both for the same finding.
The report is finished when the next person can act without asking you.

severity_ladder.level: Data loss, crash, corrupt or half-written state, silent wrong output, a security hole, or a break of a stated invariant.
A user-visible defect on a plausible input, a missing failure path, non-deterministic output, or a missing guard on a destructive action.
A defect factory. Duplication, hidden coupling, mixed responsibility, an unclear contract, or a risky path with no test.
Tidy-up with no behaviour risk. Naming, small extraction, one missing comment where the reason is not obvious.
Style a formatter or analyser already enforces. Usually do not report it at all.

verdict_rules.verdict: No P0, and at least one P1 that must land before release.
Only P2, P3, or nits remain. Say that plainly.
verdict_rules.rule: The verdict is the first line of the report. Never bury it under findings.
If the review found nothing, the verdict is "Ship" with one sentence of evidence for what you checked.

must_fix_vs_nice.must_fix: Any P0. Any P1 that can lose data or mislead a user. Any invariant break. Any untested rejection path.
must_fix_vs_nice.nice_to_have: Any P2 or P3 that can safely wait. Say when it should be paid back: next change to this file, or a named follow-up.
must_fix_vs_nice.rule: Never mix the two lists. A mixed list means nothing gets fixed in the right order.

when_to_report.case: The code can produce a wrong result for an input you can name.
A failure is hidden from the caller and from the log.
The same rule is written in two places.
A change is cheap now and expensive later.
A contract is ambiguous and two callers already disagree.
A stated repository invariant is broken.

when_to_stay_silent.case: The issue is pure taste, with no behaviour or cost argument.
A tool already reports it and CI will catch it.
You cannot say which input breaks, and cannot name the recurring cost.
The finding is far outside the review scope. Mention it once, in one line, as adjacent risk.
You would be reporting the same finding again at a second call site.
You are speculating about code you did not read.

scope_discipline.rule: Review the change. Mention adjacent risk once, in one line, and mark it as outside scope.
Do not propose a redesign to fix a small defect. Propose the smallest change that removes the harm.
Do not reopen settled decisions without new evidence. Cite the decision record if one exists.
If the change is fine but the surrounding code is not, say that first. It changes how the findings are read.

behaviour_change_labelling.rule: If the fix must change behaviour, say "Behaviour change" on its own line and state the before and after in one sentence each.
A refactor proposal names the defect class it removes and the test that proves the behaviour is unchanged.
If no test can prove equivalence, the fix is a rewrite proposal, not a refactor. Label it that way.

confidence.level: You read the line, or you saw the command output. State it.
You reasoned from code you read, without running it. Label it.
You suspect it. Write "guess" and say what would confirm it.
confidence.rule: A blocker must be a fact. An inference can be P1 at most. A guess is a question.

tradeoffs.rule: Name both sides. "Faster, but harder to test" is usable. "Better" is not.
When two options are close, recommend the one that is cheaper to change later.
Performance claims need a measurement. Without one, present the change as a hypothesis.
Readability beats cleverness unless the code is measured to be hot.

stop_and_ask.condition: The acceptance criteria are missing or contradict the code.
The fix would break a stated invariant.
The change needs a new dependency, a new permission, or a schema change.
Two sources of truth disagree and the code cannot tell you which one wins.
The behaviour can only be checked in a live host you cannot reach.
The same failure survives two evidence-led attempts.
stop_and_ask.rule: Ask one question with two to four concrete options. State the default you will take if silent.

report_shape.rule: Detail the top ten findings. One line each for the rest.
More than twenty findings: split the review by area and say which slice you covered.
Cluster duplicates under one finding with a list of sites.
Lead with the single highest risk in one sentence, even if the full list follows.
